## How Text Becomes Numbers in NLP

### Tokenization • Vocab • Embeddings • Context Windows

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Motivation

Why do LLMs need numbers?

-   Neural networks operate only on numbers\
-   Text is symbolic\
-   We must convert:\
    **Text → Tokens → Token IDs → Embeddings → Tensors**

This is the foundation of all NLP and LLMs.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Predictive Modeling Analogy

### Classical machine learning:

-   Inputs: \\(X_1, X_2, \dots, X_k\\)
-   Output: \\(y\\)

\[

\begin{bmatrix}
X_{1,1} & X_{1,2} & \dots & y_1 \\
X_{2,1} & X_{2,2} & \dots & y_2 \\
\vdots & \vdots & & \vdots \\
\end{bmatrix}

\]

### Text prediction:

-   Previous tokens → **input**\
-   Next token → **output**

\[ (t\_{i-2}, t\_{i-1}) \to t_i \]

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Tokenization Overview

**Tokenization** = splitting text into small units.

-   Word tokens\
-   Subword tokens (BPE)\
-   Characters

Models do *not* understand words.\
They understand **token IDs**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Example Sentence

**Sentence:**\
“I love large language models.”

### Word-level tokens:

1.  I\
2.  love\
3.  large\
4.  language\
5.  models\
6.  .

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Vocabulary → Token IDs

| Token    | ID  |
|----------|-----|
| I        | 1   |
| love     | 2   |
| large    | 3   |
| language | 4   |
| models   | 5   |
| .        | 6   |

Sentence →\
\[ \[1,;2,;3,;4,;5,;6\] \]

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Context Window (Small Example)

Assume: - **context length = 2**\
- Predict the next token

Examples:

| Input Tokens         | Output   |
|----------------------|----------|
| \[I, love\]          | large    |
| \[love, large\]      | language |
| \[large, language\]  | models   |
| \[language, models\] | .        |

This is exactly like a regression table.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Embedding Layer

Token IDs → embedding vectors\
Assume embedding dimension = **3**

Define an embedding matrix:

| Token    | ID  | Embedding          |
|----------|-----|--------------------|
| I        | 1   | \[0.1, 0.2, 0.3\]  |
| love     | 2   | \[-0.5, 0.1, 0.0\] |
| large    | 3   | \[0.7, -0.2, 0.4\] |
| language | 4   | \[0.0, 0.3, 0.9\]  |
| models   | 5   | \[0.4, 0.4, 0.4\]  |
| .        | 6   | \[-0.2, 0.0, 0.1\] |

Embeddings are learned during training.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Convert Tokens → Embedding Vectors

Example input:\
**X = \[I, love\] = \[1,2\]**

Embedding lookup:

-   1 → `[0.1, 0.2, 0.3]`\
-   2 → `[-0.5, 0.1, 0.0]`

Tensor shape:

**(context_length = 2) × (embed_dim = 3)**

\[

\begin{bmatrix}
0.1 & 0.2 & 0.3 \\
-0.5 & 0.1 & 0.0
\end{bmatrix}

\]

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Full Training Examples

| Tokens  | Tensor |
|---------|--------|
| \[1,2\] | \\(    |
| \[2,3\] | \\(    |
| \[3,4\] | \\(    |
| \[4,5\] | \\(    |

Target outputs:\
\[ y = \[3,4,5,6\] \]

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Next Token Prediction

The model learns:

\[ f: \mathbb{R}\^{(2 \times 3)} \to \text{Probabilities over vocabulary} \]

Outputs a distribution:

-   P(large)\
-   P(language)\
-   P(models)\
-   P(.)\
-   ...

Prediction = argmax.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Regression Analogy

| Text Modeling     | Regression                   |
|-------------------|------------------------------|
| Past tokens       | Input X                      |
| Next token        | Output y                     |
| Token IDs         | Encoded categorical features |
| Embedding vectors | Learned numeric features     |
| Context window    | Number of predictors         |
| Sequence model    | Regression function          |

LLMs = supervised learning with special input encoding.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Before Transformers

RNN/LSTM: - Reads left → right\
- Stores compressed memory\
- Struggles with long context\
- Cannot directly compare distant words

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Transformers (High-level)

Transformers take the same input tensor and add:

-   Positional encoding\
-   Multi-head self-attention\
-   Deep feedforward layers\
-   Parallel processing

But **tokenization + embeddings = the foundation**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Takeaways

-   Text must become numbers\
-   Tokenization assigns IDs\
-   Embeddings turn IDs into vectors\
-   Context window creates training examples\
-   Prediction = next token\
-   Same structure as classical prediction

------------------------------------------------------------------------
